evidence.title: What 'long tail' should you expect for your PC game in 2026?
evidence.license: Link, source identity and terse independent numerical interpretation only; article text, graphics and proprietary underlying sales estimates not copied.

claims.text: Steamworks onboarding requires electronically signed legal agreements and identity, banking and tax documentation.
claims.limitations: Requirements can depend on individual versus company status and jurisdiction; no account or tax interview undertaken.

claims.text: The payment bank account holder must match the legal name used for Steamworks enrollment; individuals can register with appropriately matching accounts.
claims.limitations: Does not establish a particular non-US bank's SWIFT capabilities or local banking eligibility.

claims.text: Valve says submitted tax information is checked through a third party and may take up to 30 days, with additional documents sometimes requested.
claims.limitations: Processing time is not a guaranteed duration and is distinct from the mandatory pre-release wait.

claims.text: Steamworks publicly specifies a USD 100 (or local equivalent) Steam Direct fee for each new app.
claims.limitations: Additional local VAT/GST and non-fee costs can apply; product-specific fees have exceptions or terms not assessed here.

claims.text: The USD 100 Steam Direct fee is not refundable but can be recouped as a distinct monthly-report line once the individual product reaches USD 1,000 in adjusted gross revenue from applicable Steam sales and in-app purchases.
claims.limitations: Recoupment is not a buyer refund, not profit and not assured for a product below the threshold.

claims.text: The Steam Direct credit cannot be purchased using Steam Wallet funds, and an existing partner must have admin permissions for the purchase.
claims.limitations: Local supported payment routes and payment-tax treatment require separately dated verification.

claims.text: The Steam Direct public enrollment page says the first titles require 30 days between payment of the app fee and release.
claims.limitations: The linked onboarding documentation contradicts it with a 21-day rule as of the same review day; do not assert this is the resolved current rule.

claims.text: The Steamworks onboarding documentation instead describes a 21-day wait after paying the app fee before that game can release.
claims.limitations: Conflicts with the Steam Direct public enrollment page saying 30 days; this may reflect differently updated documents, not independently established policy change.

claims.text: Two official Valve onboarding sources viewed October 28, 2026 report incompatible 21-day and 30-day minimum pre-release waiting periods.
claims.limitations: Exact operative rule remains unresolved; allow time for the longer stated period when constructing a hypothetical schedule but verify with Steamworks before relying on it.

claims.text: Steam requires a publicly visible Coming Soon page for at least 14 days before a new product may be released.
claims.limitations: A Coming Soon page does not prove sales, existing wishlists or a product's ability to pass build review.

claims.text: Steam's release workflow uses distinct store presence and game build checklists; the store page must be submitted for review before the build review.
claims.limitations: Applies to the documented standard release path and does not establish that every updated build needs a fresh review.

claims.text: Valve says store-page and build reviews typically take 3–5 business days each and recommends allowing at least seven business days for review contingencies.
claims.limitations: Typical review durations are neither promises nor a statement of all possible exceptions.

claims.text: After approvals and the required Coming Soon period, a developer must actively release the app via Steamworks controls; approval does not schedule automatic public sale.
claims.limitations: Not evidence of particular app launch date, customer arrival or revenue.

claims.text: The build review expects the app to launch on all supported operating systems and to implement features promised on the store page.
claims.limitations: Describes minimum review criteria only, not a guarantee of game quality or all hardware compatibility.

claims.text: Publishing the Coming Soon page or releasing an app requires both publication-change and price/discount management permissions on the relevant AppID.
claims.limitations: Does not determine partner-wide administrator roles or all financial-report access controls.

claims.text: Valve states that partner payment is issued when amounts owed for the prior sales month exceed the minimum USD 100 payment threshold.
claims.limitations: Payments require verified account banking and tax setup; no individual payee eligibility is inferred.

claims.text: Valve normally issues EFT payment toward the end of the month following the period in which the relevant sales took place.
claims.limitations: Not a guarantee of receipt date, daily liquidity, conversion spread or an individual bank's hold.

claims.text: Valve documents ACH payments to U.S. banks and USD SWIFT wires for banks outside the United States.
claims.limitations: Receiving-bank fees, countries supported and exchange conversion are not established for any specific publisher.

claims.text: Steam's near-real-time sales and activations portal reports gross revenue and units before deductions, while the monthly partner sales report includes adjustments and reflects the payment calculation.
claims.limitations: The public documentation is not an actual private merchant data export; gross count, net cash, and developed game profit must not be equated.

claims.text: Valve defines revenue-share base as gross revenue less applicable adjustments, including taxes, refunds and chargebacks, followed by the contractual revenue share and any applicable withholding.
claims.limitations: Precise partner percentage and contractual terms are not public in the examined documents; operating expenses and seller income taxes are additional unknowns.

claims.text: Valve describes VAT-inclusive storefront pricing in VAT-collecting jurisdictions, while U.S. and Canadian sales taxes, where charged, are additive at checkout.
claims.limitations: Country rates and requirements may change; does not authorize substituting a generic sales tax rate in all regions.

claims.text: Valve's tax FAQ says royalty withholding on relevant U.S.-source sales may vary from 0% to 30% according to partner tax information and treaty circumstances.
claims.limitations: Not a flat withholding on every global sale; the partner's country, submitted documents, treaty and actual tax outcome remain unknown.

claims.text: Monthly financial sales reports are available only through authenticated Steamworks partner financial-report access, not the public storefront.
claims.limitations: No partner login, privileged reports, private orders or customer records were accessed in this study.

claims.text: Valve says full releases appear in New Releases and All New Releases, with personalized and trending exposure conditional on demand.
claims.limitations: No guaranteed impressions or sales and no independent full-launch cohort.

claims.text: Valve documents separate Early Access launch and subsequent full release visibility events.
claims.limitations: One AppID must not be counted as two first commercially released games.

claims.text: Purchases and gameplay are positive qualitative signals for Steam's store recommendations.
claims.limitations: No numerical ranking weights, measured causal uplift or game-specific data.

claims.text: Steam describes supported game languages and game tags as inputs to connecting games with appropriate audiences.
claims.limitations: No uplift estimate or purchaser sample was observed.

claims.text: Wishlists generally are not direct general algorithmic ranking factors, with placements such as Popular Upcoming an exception.
claims.limitations: Personalized wishlist reminders and limited exceptions remain distinct from universal rankings.

claims.text: Valve says raw store-page traffic and page-to-purchase conversion percentages are not direct Steam store ranking factors.
claims.limitations: More traffic may indirectly produce sales that affect visibility; this does not establish zero marketing value.

claims.text: Valve says Mixed or better review score (40% positive or more) generally does not affect ranking, while a lower score may reduce featuring.
claims.limitations: Qualitative official guidance, not a validated deterministic threshold for all games.

claims.text: Valve says developers cannot purchase higher placement within Steam's organic recommendation system.
claims.limitations: Off-platform paid advertising remains a separate channel.

claims.text: Steamworks provides partner traffic analytics on impressions and visits by storefront placement.
claims.limitations: Authenticated partner reports are not public marketwide exposure statistics and none were accessed.

claims.text: A publicly visible page permits customer wishlist additions before commercial release.
claims.limitations: Wishlist is intent and notifications, not a confirmed paid sale or unique buyer.

claims.text: Steam can notify eligible wishlisters at launch, Early Access transition, or once for a qualifying free demo within a 14-day demo window.
claims.limitations: Notifications, free demo access and transition events are not paid-game sales.

claims.text: Discount notifications generally require at least 20% off, more than eight hours and inclusion of the lowest-priced package.
claims.limitations: No discount-caused sale count or commercial lift has been observed.

claims.text: Valve describes a roughly two-week per-AppID email cooldown and limits by verified emails and customer preferences.
claims.limitations: Not every person with a wishlist is guaranteed a delivered email.

claims.text: Steamworks partner reports track wishlist additions, purchases, removals and geography with next-day updates.
claims.limitations: This private data was not accessed; no actual paid-conversion share is observed.

claims.text: Valve says there is no minimum wishlist number required to appear in Steam recommendations and no universal wishlist-to-sales forecasting formula.
claims.limitations: No calibrated sales prediction, representative outcome or actual conversion denominator.

claims.text: Valve's late-2018 announced tier schedule offers publisher share of 70% on first USD 10 million, 75% on incremental revenue from USD 10 million to USD 50 million, and 80% above USD 50 million.
claims.limitations: Historical announced standard marginal terms; signed individual 2026 contracts, exceptions and exact eligible adjusted revenue have not been viewed.

claims.text: The higher publisher share after USD 10 million and USD 50 million is marginal rather than retroactively applying to preceding revenue.
claims.limitations: This is revenue, not copies, and a hypothetical schedule does not establish any developer's reported take.

claims.text: The late-November 2018 announced tier change described qualifying revenue beginning October 1, 2018 rather than counting all revenue before that date.
claims.limitations: The 2018 policy effective/accrual date is not the current operative agreement for any publisher.

claims.text: The 2018 announcement described revenue from game packages, DLC, in-game sales and game-specific Community Market fees as included in tier calculations.
claims.limitations: Not all account revenue necessarily belongs to one AppID; mapping mixed packages or parent app DLC requires separate rules.

claims.text: Valve's current finance FAQ says Game and Application AppIDs can accrue additional revenue share and DLC-only packages generally credit their parent game.
claims.limitations: This does not disclose an individual publisher's contract, net settlement or any title's qualifying tier.

claims.text: Valve says a package containing multiple Game or Application AppIDs may require manual attribution for additional revenue-share accounting.
claims.limitations: An attribution rule is not a claim of actual transaction errors or missing publisher revenue.

claims.text: Steam's published share is applied after revenue adjustments such as taxes, refunds and chargebacks, not to each gross retail checkout amount nor to net profit after production expenses.
claims.limitations: Actual tax, contractual share, holding deductions, bank fees, revenue splitting and labor costs remain unknown.

claims.text: Historical public tiers and the current Steamworks FAQ do not authenticate the exact revenue-share terms for every specific partner and game as of October 2026.
claims.limitations: No partner-only agreements or access were sought; source coverage cannot prove all exceptions absent.

claims.text: Under the 2018 standard marginal schedule a purely hypothetical $12 million of eligible adjusted revenue gives $8.5 million pre-withholding publisher share ($7 million plus $1.5 million).
claims.limitations: A mathematical illustration only; excludes withholding, external publisher splits, production expenses and excludes retail gross that has not been adjusted.

claims.text: On October 28, 2026 the live SteamDB release-summary page listed 21,224 games for release year 2025.
claims.limitations: Tracker figure is mutable and not a census of distinct publishers, paid games, sold units or buyers.

claims.text: A search result for the same SteamDB year count listed 21,228 while the opened current page displayed 21,224, showing sensitivity to crawl or refresh timing.
claims.limitations: No historical count revision ledger was captured; difference cannot be attributed to specific delistings.

claims.text: Steamlense's October 27 recalculation listed 17,651 paid-status and 2,985 free-status 2025 game releases, totaling 20,636 in its own database.
claims.limitations: Current recorded price status may differ from launch minimum; missing titles or changed release dates preclude treating this as a universal originally paid cohort.

claims.text: In its 2025 release-year cohort, steamlense reported 61.0% of tracked games under ten reviews at its October 27 snapshot.
claims.limitations: Lack of ten reviews is not absence of sales, zero earnings, owner inactivity or lack of player engagement; percentage covers paid and free games.

claims.text: Steamlense describes building its release counts from Steam API catalog information and review histories, with some desired datasets not collected.
claims.limitations: Method and coverage are supplied by the tracker and cannot independently validate every AppID or original price history.

claims.text: SteamDB and steamlense report different 2025 release totals because their recorded and classified populations are not proven identical.
claims.limitations: No row-level intersection or audit is available: subtracting counts cannot establish delisted games, omissions or paid seller numbers.

claims.text: GameDiscoverCo's July 2026 analysis selected around 5,000 games launched July 2023 through July 2025 with estimated first-month sales above 1,000 copies.
claims.limitations: The strict positive-sales eligibility rule excludes unsuccessful releases and cannot identify platform-wide game or publisher medians.

claims.text: GameDiscoverCo reported a median multiplier of 1.79 for copies from end of month one to end of year one in its selected high-selling sample.
claims.limitations: Conditional estimated cumulative multiplier, not exact audited incremental orders, comparable cash or a universal prediction.

claims.text: The same eligible sample's median gross revenue multiplier from month one to year one was about 1.67, below the copy multiplier.
claims.limitations: Revenue and unit multipliers differ; medians do not identify actual discounts, taxes, returns or publisher net bank payments.

claims.text: In the selected sample GameDiscoverCo reported median first-week-to-year-one multipliers of 2.59x for copies and 2.46x for gross revenue.
claims.limitations: Not a predictive certainty; excludes low-sales/zero titles, and sample does not supply audited checkout or rights-cleared row-level data.

claims.text: The selected-game median month-one-to-24-month cumulative unit multiplier was 2.27x.
claims.limitations: Observation horizon and sample eligibility differ from the first-week statistic; do not mix denominators for forecasts.

claims.text: Neither the success-filtered GameDiscoverCo long-tail analysis nor public catalog review-count statistics determine the fraction of all paid Steam games or publishers with no sales.
claims.limitations: Requires an eligible paid-release publisher frame including delisted zero-sale units and verifiable merchant sales or bounded estimates.

summary: Research started with public Steamworks entry, review, tax and payout documentation; detailed game sales, representative developer earnings, and paid buyer counts remain unknown.
